findings.source_passage: Yes, these eyes are windows, and this body of mine is the house. What a pity they didn't stop up the chinks and the crannies though...The universe is finished; the copestone is on, and the chips were carted off a million years ago.
findings.source_locator: paragraph beginning 'True enough, thought I, as this passage occurred to my mind'
findings.why_it_matters: This is one of the most interpretively loaded passages in the chapter — Ishmael's philosophical aside linking the body to a house, fate to finished architecture, and mortality to cosmological finality. It establishes the narrator's ironic-metaphysical voice and is a critical touchstone for readings of Ishmael's detachment and fatalism.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the full passage from 'True enough, thought I, as this passage occurred to my mind—old black-letter, thou reasonest well' through 'the chips were carted off a million years ago,' even at cost of trimming elsewhere.

findings.source_passage: Ha! thought I, ha, as the flying particles almost choked me, are these ashes from that destroyed city, Gomorrah? But 'The Crossed Harpoons,' and 'The Sword-Fish?'—this, then must needs be the sign of 'The Trap.'
findings.why_it_matters: The Gomorrah joke and the naming logic for 'The Trap' are signature Ishmaelian irony — the escalating biblical humor (Gomorrah → Tophet → The Trap) is a deliberate structural joke that the draft collapses, erasing the narrator's comic-theological voice.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the Gomorrah aside and the explicit naming of 'The Trap' with Ishmael's reasoning; this is a three-beat joke (Crossed Harpoons → Sword-Fish → The Trap/Gomorrah) that should not be compressed.

findings.source_passage: Would not Lazarus rather be in Sumatra than here? Would he not far rather lay him down lengthwise along the line of the equator; yea, ye gods! go down to the fiery pit itself, in order to keep out this frost?
findings.why_it_matters: The rhetorical escalation from Sumatra to the equator to the fiery pit is distinctively Melvillean — the hyperbolic logic that hell itself would be preferable to a New Bedford winter is a signature comic-philosophical move. The draft includes 'But what thinks Lazarus?' but omits the entire Sumatra/equator/fiery-pit sequence.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the two sentences from 'Would not Lazarus rather be in Sumatra' through 'in order to keep out this frost?' — they follow naturally from 'But what thinks Lazarus?' already present in the draft.

findings.source_passage: it seemed to have melted the packed snow and ice from before the house, for everywhere else the congealed frost lay ten inches thick in a hard, asphaltic pavement,—rather weary for me, when I struck my foot against the flinty projections, because from hard, remorseless service the soles of my boots were in a most miserable plight.
findings.source_locator: paragraph beginning 'With halting steps I paced the streets'
findings.why_it_matters: The contrast between the inn's warm glow and the asphaltic frost, plus the comic pathos of Ishmael's wrecked boot-soles, establishes his economic misery in concrete physical terms — it grounds the abstract poverty theme and provides the voice-establishing detail of self-deprecating physical comedy.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the boot-soles detail and the melted-snow/ten-inches-of-frost image; these are not merely decorative but establish Ishmael's destitution with sensory specificity.

findings.source_passage: heard a forlorn creaking in the air; and looking up, saw a swinging sign
findings.source_locator: paragraph beginning 'Moving on, I at last came to a dim sort of light'
findings.why_it_matters: 'Forlorn creaking' is a small but characteristic atmospheric touch — the sound arriving before the sight is a narrative technique Melville uses deliberately, and 'forlorn' carries tonal weight appropriate to the chapter's mood.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore 'heard a forlorn creaking in the air; and looking up' before 'saw a swinging sign.'

summary: The draft erases the chapter's most important philosophical digression ('these eyes are windows...the universe is finished'), eliminates the Gomorrah/Trap ironic naming sequence that is central to the narrator's voice, and drops the Lazarus-in-Sumatra hyperbole — together constituting two high-severity and multiple medium-severity signature losses.
